workItem.title: Invoice total off by 0.01 for some line combinations
workItem.description:
Repro steps
1. Run the API locally: dotnet run --project src/backend/Acme.Invoices.Api --launch-profile http
2. Open GET /api/invoices/17 (INV-2026-0017, Bluefen Bakery, EUR).
3. The invoice has two lines: "SMS credits, EU" 3 × 0.335 = 1.01 and "SMS credits, UK" 3 × 0.335 = 1.01.
Expected: invoice total 2.02, the sum of the line totals printed on the invoice.
Actual: invoice total 2.01.

Cause (Dana): Invoice.Total rounds the sum of the unrounded line amounts (1.005 + 1.005 = 2.010 → 2.01) instead of adding the rounded line totals (1.01 + 1.01 = 2.02).
acceptanceCriteria: The invoice total is the sum of the rounded line totals: round each line first (Money.Round), then sum.
Single-line rounding does not change (2 decimals, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero).
A unit test covers two lines of 3 × 0.335 (expected total 2.02); all existing tests stay green.

comments.author: Dana Novak
comments.text:

INV-2025-1302 2 4.0050 4.01 4.01 0.00
INV-2026-0231 4 88.0050 88.01 88.02 -0.01
INV-2026-0388 2 0.6700 0.67 0.68 -0.01
INV-2026-0402 5 120.3350 120.34 120.34 0.00
checked 182,406 invoices, 4 differ (all by -0.01), 0 differ by more
query: per-line amount = quantity * unit_price, unrounded; compared Money.Round(sum) with sum(Money.Round(line))
note: differences only appear when two or more lines end in exactly half a cent
note: no invoice is off by more than one cent; stored payments are not affected
note: Bluefen Bakery's payment of 2.02 for INV-2026-0017 is correct; the invoice total is wrong
note: the reminder email for INV-2026-0017 also quoted 2.01, because it uses the same total
runtime: 41.2s on the reporting replica, read-only, no locks taken
